title: Session planning, booking, pricing and progress records
audience: Tutors and learning-support businesses that plan sessions, set prices and report progress to families
learningOutcomes: Plan a session around one learning goal with a clear start, practice and review
Set a price and cancellation term that the family can read before paying
Write a progress note that is factual, specific and free of guarantees

instruction.heading: Planning one goal at a time
instruction.body: A session has one main learning goal, agreed with the family, written as a skill the learner will practise. The session has a short start to check previous work, a practice block, and a review at the end that the learner can explain in their own words. Plans are adjusted to the learner's progress, not to a set script.

instruction.heading: Pricing and cancellation
instruction.body: Prices, package terms and cancellation rules are written before the first session and shown to the family. Missed sessions, late cancellations and refunds are set out in plain words. The business does not promise a discount in return for a review. Where a term has consumer-law limits, the business confirms the rule before using it. UNCONFIRMED: no official source has been fetched for this point in this draft. A child-safety reviewer must confirm it before approval.

instruction.heading: Progress notes
instruction.body: A progress note records the goal, what the learner practised, what they did well, what needs more practice and the next step. It does not promise a result, compare the learner with others in a way that shames them, or describe a learning difference as a fault. Notes are shared with the family only in the agreed format and channel.

procedure: Agree one learning goal with the family and write it down
Plan the session with a start, a practice block and a review
Show the price and cancellation terms before the first payment
After each session, write a progress note with the goal, practice, strengths, next step
Share notes only in the agreed format and channel

workedExamples.situation: A parent asks for a progress note that says her child will be ready for the entrance test in six weeks. The tutor has seen steady progress but no test has been set.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What goes in the progress note?
workedExamples.reasoning: The note does not promise a test result. It records the goal, the skills practised, the progress seen, and the next steps. A time estimate is not given as a guarantee. The tutor can suggest a review point with the family.

equipmentAndPpe: Session plan template with one goal

commonErrors.error: Writing that a learner will certainly pass a test.
commonErrors.prevention: Record progress and next steps. Do not guarantee results.

commonErrors.error: Discounting in return for a review.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not offer any inducement for a review.

commonErrors.error: Describing a learning difference as a fault in a progress note.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the skill and the next step in neutral words.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Consumer law on cancellations and refunds applies and is not confirmed in this lesson. UNCONFIRMED: no official source has been fetched for this point in this draft. A child-safety reviewer must confirm it before approval.

qualityStandard: Each learner has one written goal agreed with the family
Price and cancellation terms are shown before payment
Each progress note is factual and contains no guarantee
documentationEvidence: Price and cancellation terms as shown to the family
summary: One goal per session, agreed and written
Progress notes are factual and make no guarantees

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a session plan focus on?
A parent asks for a note that guarantees a test result. What is the correct response?
options: Write it to keep the family happy
Record progress and next steps, and do not guarantee a result
Write it, but mark it as a guess
